sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#bill:

- Annual plans bill once on the enrollment date and auto-renew each year on the same date.

[Warranty Policy — Repair warranty (Meridian labor warranty) (effective 2025-06-15)]
- All repairs performed by Meridian carry a **1-year labor warranty** on the specific part repaired or replaced.
- If the same part fails within 1 year, the return visit and labor are free. Parts are covered if they were supplied by Meridian.
- The repair warranty does not cover different components, pre-existing conditions noted on the original invoice, or failures caused by lack of maintenance, power surges, or customer modifications.

sections.faq/customer_faq.md#scheduling-0:
[Meridian Home Comfort — Customer FAQ — Scheduling (effective 2026-03-02)]
- Standard appointment windows are 8am–12pm, 12pm–4pm, and 1pm–5pm. A 4pm–7pm window is available Tuesday and Thursday only.
- You will receive a text the morning of your appointment with the technician's name and photo, and another text when the tech is 30 minutes away.
- Cancellations or reschedules more than 24 hours before the window are free. Inside 24 hours there is a $49 late-cancellation fee. No-shows (nobody home at the address) are charged the full diagnostic fee.
sections.services/technician_arrival_and_etas.md#:
[Technician Arrival Windows and Delays]
Appointment windows are 4-hour blocks. Technicians arrive at any point within the window.
If a technician is running late:
1. Dispatch will text the customer with an updated ETA.
2. If the technician will miss the window entirely, the customer can reschedule at no charge.
Customers are not required to wait past the window. A missed window is never charged as a no-show.

sections.services/technician_arrival_and_etas.md#:
[Technician Arrival Windows and Delays]
Appointment windows are 4-hour blocks. Technicians arrive at any point within the window.
If a technician is running late:
1. Dispatch will text the customer with an updated ETA.
2. If the technician will miss the window entirely, the customer can reschedule at no charge.
Customers are not required to wait past the window. A missed window is never charged as a no-show.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

Do you want to try these first, or should I find you an appointment now?

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

transcript: caller: I'm calling to book a repair, the furnace won't kick on.

agent: Sorry to hear that. I can help get a repair booked. First I need to verify your account: please give me your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address.

agent: Thanks, Jennifer, you're verified. Before I book, here are a few quick checks that sometimes fix this:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above the room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (it looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.

If you ever smell gas, stop right away and follow the gas safety protocol. If you've already tried these or would rather skip them, I'll find you an appointment.
caller: I already checked the thermostat and it's set to heat. I haven't checked the other things. I'd rather just book the visit, so please go ahead and schedule it. The unit is a Trane.

3. Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski

agent: I don't have anything open tomorrow. The earliest I can offer is Monday, Oct 19. These are the options now:

caller: Yes, I'll take the 12pm-4pm slot on Monday, Oct 19. Ray Mendoza is fine. Please go ahead and book it.
agent: You're booked, Jennifer: Monday, Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, for a furnace repair with technician Ray Mendoza. You can tell him it's a Trane unit when he arrives.
caller: Thanks. Before you finish up, do I need to pay anything for this visit?
agent: There's an $89 diagnostic fee for the visit. If you approve the repair during that same visit, it's credited toward the repair cost. It's waived for Comfort Club members.

- Members may cancel auto-renewal at any time before the renewal date.
- Annual plans are non-refundable once a tune-up has been performed in the current term.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.services/service_catalog.md#maintenance-:

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

sections.faq/customer_faq.md#payment-0:
[Meridian Home Comfort — Customer FAQ — Payment (effective 2026-03-02)]
- We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, and ACH.
- We do not accept checks or cash from technicians in the field.
- Card numbers are never taken over the phone. Agents send a secure payment link by text or email, valid for 24 hours.
- Financing is available on repairs over $1,000 and all system replacements through our financing partner. Approval takes about 5 minutes.
sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#bill:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan — Billing and renewal (effective 2026-01-01)]
- Annual plans bill once on the enrollment date and auto-renew each year on the same date.
- Monthly plans bill on the enrollment day of each month and require a 12-month minimum commitment.
- Members receive a renewal reminder email 30 days before renewal.
- Existing members are locked at their enrollment price until their next renewal date, at which point the current price applies.
sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#repair-warra:
[Warranty Policy — Repair warranty (Meridian labor warranty) (effective 2025-06-15)]
- All repairs performed by Meridian carry a **1-year labor warranty** on the specific part repaired or replaced.
- If the same part fails within 1 year, the return visit and labor are free. Parts are covered if they were supplied by Meridian.
- The repair warranty does not cover different components, pre-existing conditions noted on the original invoice, or failures caused by lack of maintenance, power surges, or customer modifications.
sections.faq/customer_faq.md#duplicate-charges-0:
[Meridian Home Comfort — Customer FAQ — Duplicate charges (effective 2026-03-02)]
If you see two charges, one is usually a pending authorization that drops off in 3–5 business days. If both post, contact us and we will open a case with our payment processor.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

turns.caller: What does the Comfort Club membership actually include?

It also includes $500 off a full system replacement. Comfort Club Plus ($269/year) adds an annual water heater flush and inspection, a whole-home plumbing inspection, and 15% off plumbing repairs.

turns.caller: The AC. It just stopped running. The fan doesn't come on at all when I set it to cool.
turns.agent:
Here are a few quick checks to try first:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to COOL, with the set point below the room temperature.
2. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
3. Look at the outdoor unit. If it's covered in debris or its fan isn't spinning, book a visit.
4. Check the air filter and replace it if it's dirty.

Have you already tried these, or would you like me to book the warranty diagnostic visit now?

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Look at the outdoor unit. If it's covered in debris or the fan isn't spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

caller: Tomorrow isn't open, so I'll take the earliest one. Option 1, Mon Oct 19, 12pm to 4pm with Tasha Bell, works for me.
agent: Just to confirm: book Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit, technician Tasha Bell?
caller: Yes, please book that one.

agent: You're booked, Grace. Tasha Bell will come Monday, October 19, between 12pm and 4pm for the repair visit. Your warranty claim is under way. There's no diagnostic fee if the technician confirms the failure is covered. You can tell Tasha about anything else on arrival.

sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#intr:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan (effective 2026-01-01)]
The Comfort Club is Meridian's annual maintenance membership for residential HVAC systems.
sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#comf:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan — Comfort Club (Standard) (effective 2026-01-01)]
- Price: **$189 per year** per system, or **$16.99 per month**
- Each additional system on the same address: **$99 per year**
- Includes:
  - Two seasonal tune-ups per year (one cooling, one heating)
  - Priority scheduling — members are booked ahead of non-members
  - Diagnostic fee ($89) waived on all service calls
  - 15% off all repairs (parts and labor)
  - No after-hours dispatch fee on emergency calls
  - Annual reminder and filter-change notifications
sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#bill:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan — Billing and renewal (effective 2026-01-01)]
- Annual plans bill once on the enrollment date and auto-renew each year on the same date.
- Monthly plans bill on the enrollment day of each month and require a 12-month minimum commitment.
- Members receive a renewal reminder email 30 days before renewal.
- Existing members are locked at their enrollment price until their next renewal date, at which point the current price applies.
sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#comf:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan — Comfort Club Plus (effective 2026-01-01)]
- Price: **$269 per year** per system
- Everything in Standard, plus:
  - Annual water heater flush and inspection
  - Annual whole-home plumbing inspection
  - 15% off plumbing repairs
  - $500 off any full system replacement (Standard members also receive this)

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
